messages:
sam: heads-up — multiple customers hit JIT onboarding failures after the RBAC change rolled yesterday. Users are auto-provisioned but landing in the 'guest' bucket instead of their expected roles. can we triage?

marta: seeing this too. quick glance shows our role map now requires attribute 'employeeType' for tenant-admin. a subset of AD->Okta federated users don't have that claim in their SAML assertion. :confused:

devon: digging into logs. okta_trace: https://okta.example/trace/3f2b1c — error in our-onboard-service: "missing required role attribute: employeeType". attaching a trimmed SAML assertion sample: 
```
<AttributeStatement>
  <Attribute Name=\"email\">user@acme.com</Attribute>
  <Attribute Name=\"givenName\">Jill</Attribute>
  <!-- employeeType missing for these accounts -->
</AttributeStatement>
```

okta-bot: session_logged user=user@acme.com, result=success, attributes_provided=[email,givenName]

marta: also found a weird KMS decryption log for private deployments where the CMK tag lookup returned a different tag set. our KMS key tagging changed last week (we added tag key_tag=infra) and the assert-to-key mapping in the private agent expects key_tag=platform. fallback behavior currently returns a cached ephemeral guest key. that explains guest role + missing audit detail. :lock:

devon: so two orthogonal failures: missing SAML attr for RBAC mapping + KMS tag mismatch causing wrong key resolution during onboarding. both lead to degraded role assignment.

sam: priority: 1) stop new users being mis-assigned, 2) ensure audit logs show clearly why fallback happened, 3) provide remediation for users already wrong. plan?

marta: temp mitigation: revert the strict 'employeeType required' check in role-mapper to allow email_verified path and emit an audit event with reason="attr_missing". PR coming. will also add a rate-limited metric for attr_missing_count.

devon: agree. for KMS: we should add a tolerant lookup that checks both tag variants and emit an audit/a11y event when tag mismatch detected. patch in private-agent to try both tags before falling back.

sam: ok, approve rollback + logging change. we'll ship hotfix to hosted and private. can we avoid full revert so we still get telemetry on attr deficiency?

marta: yes — implement as: allow fallback, but create an AuditEvent: "RBAC_FALLBACK", fields: [user, missing_attrs, resolved_key_tags, fallback_reason]. a sample event: 
```
RBAC_FALLBACK user=user@acme.com missing_attrs=[employeeType] resolved_key_tags=[platform->not_found, infra->found] fallback_reason="kms_tag_mismatch"
```

devon: I'll add a migration job: run SCIM enrichment for users with missing employeeType (map from AD.department -> employeeType where possible) and mark records with migration_ts. this will reduce recurrence. job runs as low-priority background task.

oncall: created incident INC-2023-981, paged oncall rotation, added runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/ops/rbac-jit-onboard. current severity: P2 until we validate rollback across tenants.

sam: timeline?

marta: patch branch created, tests added. will cut release in 30m to staging, smoke for 10m, then prod.

devon: migration job ready for manual trigger after patch; will run in waves (1000 users / hr) to avoid SCIM throttles.

sam: great. after patch, we need an audit sweep: query AuditEvents for RBAC_FALLBACK in last 24h and notify affected customers with remediation steps. legal/compliance copy needed.

marta: noted, will include sample log lines and query saved filter.

devon: one more — add a small healthcheck alert: if attr_missing_rate > 0.5% over 5m on any tenant, auto-open a ticket. avoids regressions from future RBAC changes.

sam: perfect. thanks. keep updates here and ping when prod roll is done. :eyes:
